answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by binding each identity to a costly proof-of-work ledger write, so mass-cloning identities would require prohibitive compute. Yet expense alone is not enough: a lightweight attestation kernel verifies that human-backed agents sign their work cryptographically, and reputation decays if credentials go stale. Like a falcon hunting in a wide sky, the network targets the cheapest clones first, pruning them before they can collude. Thus every new identity must forge its history from real, referenced labor, making fake swarms economically irrational.
